## LLM011 New ChatClient/ChatModel per request

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Level | error |
| Framework | Both |
| Autofix | no patch; fix it by hand as described below |
| More | https://github.com/pgy763/llm-lint/blob/main/docs/rules.md#llm011 |
| Turn it off | `LLM011: off` in .llm-lint.yml, or `--disable LLM011` on the command line |

Spring AI's ChatClient/ChatModel and LangChain4j's ChatLanguageModel are build-once-use-many objects: they carry a connection pool and a retryer inside. Building them in a business method reopens the pool and redoes the TLS handshake on every request; under load threads and ports are exhausted first.

To mute it in one place, put `// llm-lint:ignore LLM011` on that line or the line above.
<!-- /generated:llm011 -->

## What it looks like

`ChatClient.builder(...)` or `new OpenAiChatModel(...)` inside a request-handling method.

## How to fix

Build the client once in a `@Bean` or the constructor and inject it. A client per request re-creates HTTP pools and loses connection reuse.
